speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your blood pressure and check for secondary causes of hypertension. How old are you, and do you have any symptoms like headaches, vision changes, or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history, but I need to confirm your blood pressure readings from today. Can you describe if you have ever felt dizzy, had headaches, or noticed any swelling in your legs or face? REQUEST TEST: Blood pressure measurement (upper and lower extremities).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood pressure 150/80 mm Hg in the right upper extremity; lower extremity blood pressure is lower than upper extremity values (differential noted). Patient is asymptomatic with no reported dizziness, headaches, or swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood pressure results confirm significant hypertension in both arms and legs. Given your age and the severity of the findings, I need to check for physical signs of renal issues. Do you have any family history of kidney disease or early heart attacks? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Serum Creatinine. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Normal; Serum Creatinine: Normal; Abdominal Ultrasound: Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal renal function and imaging, primary hypertension is unlikely; I need to rule out cardiac causes. Do you ever experience chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations? REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG). REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrocardiogram: Normal sinus rhythm, left ventricular hypertrophy present. Echocardiogram: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy, and the echocardiogram confirms narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, which is the definitive finding for your condition. This obstruction causes high blood pressure in the upper body and forces the left ventricle to work harder.
